sentences.text: This animal belongs to the genus Spinophorosaurus, with the species name nigerensis, both established by Remes and colleagues in 2009.
The generic name translates to 'spine-bearing lizard,' a reference to what were initially thought to be spiked osteoderms, while the specific name indicates the discovery location.

The subadult holotype — the specimen the species is based on — measured approximately 13 meters in length, whereas the paratype reached about 14 meters, with both individuals standing roughly 4 meters tall at the shoulder.
German explorers Ulrich Joger and Edgar Sommer explored the semi-deserts south of Agadez in early 2005, where Joger found a complete femur during a one-hour search.
With assistance from local Tuaregs, the pair uncovered most of the holotype specimen after two days, leading to its formal designation in 2009.
One study suggests Spinophorosaurus may have been a high browser.
The parent group of Spinophorosaurus is Gravisauria.

Spinophorosaurus was a sauropod dinosaur that lived in present-day Niger during the Middle Jurassic, specifically within the Irhazer Shale formation from the Bajocian to Bathonian stages, between 170.9 and 165.3 million years ago.

It is debated whether Spinophorosaurus is a very basal sauropod or belongs inside Eusauropoda. In 2013, researchers reexamined supposed tail spikes and found they lacked the typical rugose surface of osteoderms or the club-like expansion seen in Shunosaurus, doubting whether the supposed tail spikes were of different sizes as originally proposed due to their broken edges. Several subsequent studies suggested a basal position outside Eusauropoda, placing Spinophorosaurus as the sister taxon of Tazoudasaurus or Volkheimeria.
